title: Lowering edge connectivity by deleting one edge
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph whose edge connectivity satisfies $\kappa'(G) = k+1$ for some natural number $k$. Then $G$ has an edge $e$ whose deletion yields a graph $G - e$ with $\kappa'(G - e) = k$.
hypotheses_covered: edge connectivity of G equals k+1
replaced:
Successor step, part 1: from a minimum edge cut of size \texttt{k + 1}, deleting one
of its edges drops the edge connectivity to exactly \texttt{k}.
